Limb (b) is not met: the driver answered 'at the block' at 20:23:40, 25 seconds later and well inside the 120-second window, and the clause provides that where the driver did reply within 120 seconds it does not apply regardless of the content of the reply. The rider's exoneration must therefore come from the failure of POL-NS-01 limb (b), which the absent trace supplies.

ledger.claim: The platform's own trip record for TRP-00411 carries a driver 'arrived' event at 20:21:45 and a driver termination at 20:27:45 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW with cancelled_by DRIVER and no boarding event anywhere — 360 seconds on the clock, which exceeds the 300-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 300; no_show_threshold_sec is null, so no longer threshold applies). POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are therefore made out on the face of the record, and the arrived event is the only arrival clock this trip carries, because EV-GPS-00411 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and no in-geofence fix exists from which limb (c) could be re-run.

EV-GPS-00411 is MISSING, carries no payload and has weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT: the platform holds no GPS record between acceptance and cancellation. Under POL-GEN-02(3) a MISSING artifact can carry no fact, and POL-NS-02's own treatment of unusable positioning — fixes worse than 25 m accuracy 'count as evidence of neither presence nor absence' — shows the drafters' method for unusable positioning is to neuter it, not to convert it into absence. A trace that does not exist contains no fix, and the gap in the platform's telemetry cannot be read as an affirmative finding that this driver was outside the 50 m STANDARD radius. The rider's 'there was no car at my block' must rest on something, and no admissible artifact in this bundle places the driver anywhere at any time.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider. The rider's only message, 'where? i dont see' at 20:23:15, was answered by the driver at 20:23:40 — 25 seconds later, far inside the 120-second window of limb (b) — so the clause does not apply regardless of the content of the reply; the empty in_app_calls list therefore does not assist the rider either. What the chat actually shows is a driver who messaged 'here' 20 seconds after the arrival event and who was still answering the rider's query 6 minutes after acceptance, and a rider who named no block, entrance, tower or bay identifier even when directly asked where they were. Limb (i) of POL-NS-03's fault allocation therefore finds nothing to pin on this driver.

Rider presence under POL-NS-04(c) cannot be run at all: EV-GPS-00411 carries no rider_track because it carries no payload (MISSING, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT). POL-NS-11 is explicit that this makes limb (c) UNDECIDABLE — neither satisfied nor failed — that POL-NS-04 accordingly cannot exonerate the rider, and that the missing rider track does not impair the evidence of the driver's arrival or dwell and does not by itself engage POL-NS-08(b) or POL-NS-09(e). The rider's own device recorded nothing, and the rider cannot convert that into a finding in their favour.

POL-NS-06 gives the rider nothing here because there is no shortfall to compute: the effective waiting interval on the record runs 360 seconds against the 300-second minimum, and the driver cancelled 60 seconds AFTER the minimum had elapsed (20:27:45 against 20:26:45). The clause's summation limb (i) is beside the point — and in any event EV-ADVIS-00411-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT: no advisory covers Geylang Bahru in this window), so no party on either side can assert a kerbside restriction, closure or enforcement event on this pickup road.

The false-arrival route of POL-NS-05 has no trigger on this record. The clause fires only where the arrival timestamp can be matched to a GPS fix placing the driver more than 300 m from the pin, or showing motion at 15 km/h or more; EV-GPS-00411 (MISSING, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) supplies no fix at the arrival time or at any other time, so neither trigger can be shown and no false-arrival referral can properly be recorded against this driver. The rider's account of a driver who said 'here' without being there is an assertion with no artifact behind it, and POL-NS-05(iii) confirms that even a false marker would not defeat a fee whose corrected dwell meets the minimum.

The money follows from POL-NS-07. POL-NS-01 being satisfied and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, the driver is compensated at 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee in force for this trip — SGD 3.20, which is exactly the driver_compensation figure the fare_breakdown's own derived money block computes here. The anti-farming check does not trip on either limb: no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below 4) and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 120 is 0.008 (below 0.08), so compensation is NOT withheld, and no POL-NS-09 profile trigger is engaged either (rider no_show_disputes_30d 0; disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0 on both sides). Per POL-NS-07 and POL-GEN-03 the emitted ruling on such a case is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd — the disposition of the fee is that it stands, not a rider refund.

The dispute is rider-filed and the ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and total_charged SGD 4.00, which reconciles exactly with the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee in platform_policy for this trip — so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect and the ledger carries full weight. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION means the filing party's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state STANDS: nothing in this bundle supports moving that SGD 4.00 back to the rider, and the fee is already where it should be.

Fallback, on the bench's own arithmetic rather than mine: if arrival is held not to be verifiable because the platform's telemetry failed, that is a gap, not a finding that the driver was elsewhere, and the fee must not be refunded on the strength of it. On that footing the only evidence for the deciding fact is the absent trace itself — a trace with no fixes is a trace with fewer than six across the waiting window — so POL-NS-09 is the disposal and its effect is to HOLD the disputed SGD 4.00 rather than collect or refund it, and escalation is TERMINAL: the rider's claim is not paid out in the meantime, and the human reviewer decides on the platform's own arrival and wait-timer record.

Finally, the rider has already paid — payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 on EV-FARE-00411 — so a held fee leaves the rider out of pocket pending review, whereas FULL_REFUND is the only disposition that returns the contested $4.00.

discarded_claims.claim: The absent rider_track must not be converted into an adverse finding or an escalation against the rider. POL-NS-11 provides that where POL-NS-04 limb (c) cannot be run the test is UNDECIDABLE — neither satisfied nor failed — and that, notwithstanding POL-NS-08(b), the missing rider_track is not the evidence for any deciding fact of the remaining clauses, does not by itself engage POL-NS-08(b) or POL-NS-09(e), and does not lower the cap on a finding that rests on the driver's track. The rider is not required to prove where she was standing; the fee turns on where the driver was, and on this record that is unproven by the trace POL-NS-01 requires and by every other admissible artifact.

discarded_claims.claim: Fallback, on the bench's own arithmetic rather than mine: if arrival is held not to be verifiable because the platform's telemetry failed, that is a gap, not a finding that the driver was elsewhere, and the fee must not be refunded on the strength of it. On that footing the only evidence for the deciding fact is the absent trace itself — a trace with no fixes is a trace with fewer than six across the waiting window — so POL-NS-09 is the disposal and its effect is to HOLD the disputed SGD 4.00 rather than collect or refund it, and escalation is TERMINAL: the rider's claim is not paid out in the meantime, and the human reviewer decides on the platform's own arrival and wait-timer record.

ruling.explanation:
This case cannot be decided on the record and goes to a human reviewer. The disputed S$4.00 cancellation fee for TRP-00411 is held — not collected and not refunded — until that review is complete.

What the record shows. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00411, weight 1.0) carries a driver-pressed 'arrived' marker at 20:21:45 and a driver cancellation at 20:27:45 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding event: 360 seconds, longer than the 300-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec; the 180-second default does not apply, and no_show_threshold_sec is null). The chat log (EV-CHAT-00411, weight 1.0) shows 'here' at 20:22:05, 'where? i dont see' at 20:23:15 and 'at the block' at 20:23:40 — three messages, matching trip_record.chat_message_count, so no chat defect under POL-NS-08(c). The fare ledger (EV-FARE-00411, weight 1.0) shows a S$4.00 cancellation-fee line equal to platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of S$4.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd S$0.00, so there is no fare defect under POL-NS-08(d).

Why the case cannot be decided. POL-NS-01 makes the fee chargeable only if all four limbs hold. Limbs (a) and (d) are made out on the trip record alone, but limb (b) is decided by the gps_trace, and EV-GPS-00411 is MISSING — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, payload null (named as POL-GEN-02(3) requires). There is no qualifying in-geofence fix within the 50 m STANDARD radius at any time, because there is no fix at all. Under POL-NS-02 a trace that cannot establish the in-radius readings is impaired rather than proof of absence, so the geofence test could not be run: limb (b) is neither satisfied nor failed. Limb (c)'s dwell runs from the first qualifying in-geofence fix and so never starts; the 360 seconds between two driver-set markers cannot stand in for a GPS-measured dwell. POL-NS-12 supplies nothing here: it applies only where arrival_marker is GPS_AUTO and the record carries the platform's own arrival event with wait_timer_started and wait_timer_expired, and this record has arrival_marker BUTTON and no events array, so there is no platform-confirmed arrival independent of the export. The driver's account ('I was at Blk 51 ... waited six minutes') is offered in the place of the test that admitted no reading; it does not supply the missing measurement, does not lift the confidence cap, and does not stop the absent trace being the only evidence of where the vehicle was.

Consequence. The sole evidence for the deciding fact — the driver's position during the waiting window — is the impaired trace, so the confidence cap is its weight of 0.0 (POL-GEN-02(2)), below the 0.70 confidence floor, and POL-NS-09(e) applies as well. POL-NS-09 is terminal: no monetary ruling issues, the S$4.00 is held, and no referral is produced because no clause here produces one.

The claims, answered. The rider's argument that 'no qualifying fix' from an absent trace makes limb (b) fail and earns a full refund is rejected: a test that could not be run is not evidence the driver was elsewhere (POL-NS-02's sparse-trace sentence; POL-NS-11). POL-NS-06 cannot refund the fee either, because it needs the dwell computed under POL-NS-02 and there is no dwell to compute; the missing advisory EV-ADVIS-00411-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) makes limb (i) unavailable in any event. POL-NS-05 records no false-arrival referral, because neither trigger (over 300 m from the pin, or motion at 15 km/h or more) can be shown without a fix. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider — the driver replied 25 seconds after her message, inside the 120-second window — which the rider fairly concedes, and rider presence is undecidable under POL-NS-11. The driver's POL-NS-07 claim for S$3.20 is not payable: POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and limbs (b) and (c) cannot be established; the anti-farming check does not trip in any event (1 no-show termination in 30 days against a threshold of 4; 1/120 = 0.008 against 0.08), so nothing under POL-NS-09(c) or (d) is engaged either.

Open question for the reviewer: whether the platform's own full-resolution location stream for TRP-00411 places the driver inside the 50 m pickup radius around 20:21:45 to 20:27:45, and for how long continuously. That measurement — a record-type item either party may add under POL-GEN-04(b) — decides the case: a qualifying in-geofence dwell of 300 seconds or more from the first qualifying fix means the fee stands and S$3.20 is payable to the driver; no qualifying fix means the S$4.00 is refunded in full to the rider. The amount is below the S$8.00 automatic-execution threshold, but as no monetary ruling issues it stays held pending review.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
